per_window.ps-ns: not_measured: the spin-relaxation search found no R1/NOE/S2 study of VHR, and the 2020 paper reports none (VHR-J10).
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window: apo WT at 25 °C, nine VI and acid-loop amides fit one process with kex 1530 ± 200 s-1 and pA 98.8 ± 0.1% (VHR-J1, r1); a Hahn-echo survey of the same apo state adds exchange at the alpha7 site and other residues, 14 in all (VHR-J2, r2). Tungstate-bound WT keeps a similar profile (VHR-J3, r3). N74A mutant data show more broadening in apo and tungstate-bound forms (VHR-J4, J5; r4, r5; inference_from_mutant). A 2017 qualitative statement of acid-loop motion has no retrievable data and stays unresolved (VHR-J6, r8, indirect). Single temperature only; the RelaxDB source dissertation was not read (VHR-J12, search_insufficient).
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured: HDX-MS, EPR/DEER, smFRET, time-resolved and multitemperature structural methods and CEST were searched with no hits (VHR-J11).
per_window.undetermined: Apo crystals 8TK6/9DJ9 at 100 K superpose closely in the acid loop and P-loop (VHR-J8, r10, r11, structure_only, no_evidence_in_window). The F17 complex shifts the VI E-loop (A63-N72) by up to 1.4 Å and moves R125 (VHR-J9, r9, unresolved). Tungstate-bound MD over 150 ns shows a more open acid loop in WT than in N74A (VHR-J7, r6, md_only). Not judged: alanine-scan CSP mapping (r7, mutants, no timescale); F19 distal-site crystal (r12); ligand-observed 19F CPMG screen in PBS (r13, reports fragment binding, not protein exchange); SA3 complex of the 3-185 construct versus C124S peptide complex (r14); peptide-orientation MD (r15); cross-linking dimerization, abstract only (r16); C124S peptide complex, abstract only (r17).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 25 °C (pH 6.5, phosphate-free Bis-Tris propane buffer, deuterated sample) free wild-type VHR exchanges on the millisecond scale in the variable insert (A63, R66, N72) and the acid loop (K89, D92, E95, F96, L98, S99), which fit one shared process with kex 1530 ± 200 s-1 and a minor-state population of about 1.2% (pA 98.8 ± 0.1%); the minor state's structure is unknown and its shifts do not match the tungstate-bound state, and no other temperature or method has measured it.
open_conflicts: Same apo 25 °C CPMG data, two models: separate fits give acid loop kex 1400 ± 200 s-1, pA 98.9 ± 0.1% and VI kex 2100 ± 460 s-1, pA 98.5 ± 0.4%, while the authors prefer one combined fit (kex 1530 ± 200 s-1, pA 98.8 ± 0.1%) on AIC/F-test grounds (r1); the coupling claim rests on that model choice.

Same apo sample, two exchange methods: Hahn-echo Rex agrees with CPMG Rex within error for seven of eight shared residues but not for D92, and Hahn-echo flags six residues (R36, Y78, R119, C124, G161, D164) that were not in the CPMG fit (r1, r2).
CPMG constant relaxation time for the same 2020 experiment: 40 ms in the publisher PDF (Methods) versus 30 ms in the cached PMC author-manuscript text; r1 now records both.
questions_for_gina: Which data set is the RelaxDB VHR_CPMG entry: the 2020 paper's 700 μM deuterated apo sample at 25 °C (600/700/800 MHz), or a different dissertation sample (Table 7.10.3, 800 MHz only)? If different, what temperature and buffer did it use?

Should the atlas carry the combined VI + acid-loop fit (kex 1530 s-1) as the WT apo answer, or keep the separate acid-loop (1400 s-1) and VI (2100 s-1) fits as equally valid until a second temperature or method tests the coupling?
protein_summary.buffer_note: All 2020 NMR samples (r1-r5) used 20 mM Bis-Tris propane, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 1 mM EDTA, 7% D2O and NaN3 printed as '2%' (the 2017 preparation lists 0.02%; not corrected), pH 6.5; the Hahn-echo samples were 700 or 965 μM enzyme, not mapped to each state. The apo samples (r1, r2, r5) had no added phosphate, so phosphate binding is not a concern for the apo exchange; the authors' own titration shows phosphate binds the P-loop and perturbs shifts out to the VI and alpha7. Untested conditions: a single temperature (25 °C), EDTA throughout, perdeuteration, and no buffer comparison. The 19F fragment screen (r13) ran in PBS, and the crystals (r9-r12) are at 100 K in Bis-Tris/NH4F/PEG, and a phosphate-bound structure (8TK4) was also solved.
